common.tagline: Understand your symptoms. Know your next step.

disclaimer.bannerText: Educational health triaging only. Not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. In an emergency, dial 112 immediately.

emergency.title: Emergency Medical Help
emergency.subtitle: If you or someone nearby is experiencing life-threatening symptoms, call emergency services immediately.
emergency.redFlagChest: Crushing chest pain, chest tightness, or pain spreading to arm or jaw
emergency.redFlagBreathing: Severe breathing difficulty, choking, or gasping for breath
emergency.redFlagStroke: Sudden facial drooping, speech difficulty, or weakness on one side
emergency.redFlagBleeding: Heavy uncontrollable bleeding, coughing or vomiting blood
emergency.redFlagConsciousness: Loss of consciousness, unresponsive, or active convulsions/seizures
emergency.redFlagSelfHarm: Thoughts of self-harm, suicide, or acute psychological crisis
emergency.whatToDoTitle: What to do while waiting for help
emergency.step1: Stay calm and keep the person still. Do not move someone who may have an injury.
emergency.step2: Clear space around the person. If unconscious but breathing, place in recovery position.
emergency.step3: Unlock doors and assign someone to wait outside to guide the ambulance crew.

landing.heroTitle: Clear, calm health guidance when you need it most.
landing.heroSubtitle: SafeSteps helps you assess your symptoms, understand clinical urgency, and know the right next step to take.
landing.howItWorksStep1Desc: Describe symptoms in your own words. We ask calm, structured questions.
landing.howItWorksStep2Desc: Our verified medical knowledge base evaluates potential causes and red flags.
landing.howItWorksStep3Desc: Know whether to seek emergency care, see a GP soon, or manage safely at home.
landing.safetyDesc: SafeSteps never prescribes medication doses, never guesses lab values, and always prioritises your safety.
landing.urgencyEmergencyDesc: Life-threatening symptoms requiring immediate ambulance attendance (112).
landing.urgencyDoctorSoonDesc: Symptoms needing medical evaluation within 24 to 48 hours.
landing.urgencySelfCareDesc: Mild symptoms manageable with rest, hydration, and monitoring.
